errors.english: how could the intellect of women who conquer men apply to those possessed of such glory?
errors.why: The verse (Skt strījitānāṃ matiḥ kutaḥ) asks what wisdom those conquered by women have, bowing as they do to the glorious; it is not the intellect of women who conquer men.

fix.find: how could the intellect of women who conquer men apply to those possessed of such glory?
fix.replace: what wisdom is there in those conquered by women, who bow before the glorious?

note: The narrative verses (fratricide, thumb wound, Arthadatta's ship) are faithful; the gnomic verse on men ruled by women is inverted.
A careful rendering of the dream/waking argument and the debate on the universal of cognition, with verse and commentary kept apart.

errors.english: Whatever touches exceptionally pure silk, sweet-scented flowers, honey, or saffron instantly becomes foul.
errors.why: It is the pure silk, flowers, honey and saffron that instantly become impure wherever they touch the body, not whatever touches them.

fix.find: Whatever touches exceptionally pure silk, sweet-scented flowers, honey, or saffron instantly becomes foul.
fix.replace: Exceptionally pure silk, sweet-scented flowers, honey, or saffron instantly become foul wherever they touch it.

note: The meditation on the foulness of the body and on 'I' and 'mine' reads faithfully apart from one inverted line.

errors.english: Does one intend to establish the act of speaking itself as an independent thesis
errors.why: སྨྲ་བ་ཉིད (vaktṛtva, 'being a speaker') is the reason used in an independent (svatantra) inference, not a thesis to be established.

errors.english: if one does not analyze it, it appears pleasant
errors.why: 'Pleasing only when unexamined' qualifies the mere scripture from which the property is known to the opponent; it does not describe the prasaṅga itself.

errors.english: when you assert that all wandering beings are ultimately one
errors.why: In this answer to the Aupaniṣadas, འགྲོ་བ་ཐམས་ཅད means the whole world (jagat), all things, which is said to be one; it does not mean sentient beings.

note: The outline is followed, but the vaktṛtva argument and the Advaita monism are blurred in places.

errors.english: this is the sixty-first branch, entitled *The Story of the Farmer*
errors.why: This is the closing colophon of chapter 61 (continuing the ཅེས་པ on the previous side), not a title for the following story of Suprabuddha, which begins a new chapter.

fix.find: this is the sixty-first branch, entitled *The Story of the Farmer*
fix.replace: here ends the sixty-first branch, *The Story of the Farmer*

note: The opening verses of the new avadāna are rendered well; the preceding chapter's colophon is presented as a heading.
The praise verses of the Vinaya and their commentary are rendered faithfully, with verse and gloss kept distinct.

errors.english: Those who dwell in the teachings will ask how such qualities could possibly exist or not exist today, and even executioners will be sent forth.
errors.why: The degenerate monks, saying that such qualities do not exist at all today, will even send executioners against those who abide by the Dharma (ལ marks the target); the Dharma-abiders are not the ones speaking.

fix.find: Those who dwell in the teachings will ask how such qualities could possibly exist or not exist today, and even executioners will be sent forth.
fix.replace: Saying that such qualities do not exist at all today, they will even send executioners against those who abide by the teachings.

errors.english: No karmic ripening shall result from their actions.
errors.why: The point is that their karma will not ripen on me (each owns his own karma); it does not say that their deeds have no ripening at all.
གདོལ་པ is caṇḍāla (an outcaste), not a hunter.

note: The verses are read fluently as prose, but the persecution verse misplaces who speaks and who is attacked.

errors.why: རྗེས་སུ་འཇུག་པའི་ཤེས་པ is anuvṛtti-pratyaya, the recurrent or inclusive cognition of sameness across individuals, not a 'sequential' cognition (the same misreading gives 'applied consecutively' above).
སྤྱི་བརྩལ་ནས means 'in general terms', contrasted with ཁྱད་པར་སྒྲུབ་ན ('if you prove a specific one'); it does not mean setting aside the universal.

errors.english: cognitions such as that of a "cooker" would be erroneous
errors.why: The reason would be inconclusive (deviating, vyabhicāra) because of the cognitions of 'cooker' and the like; it does not say that those cognitions are erroneous.

note: The overall apoha argument comes through, but key logical terms (anuvṛtti, the general/specific dilemma, vyabhicāra) are mistranslated.

errors.english: just as space and other unconditioned phenomena do not arise without a cause
errors.why: Space is the example of what is uncaused and therefore never arises; uncaused arising is untenable, and the English implies that space arises with a cause.

note: A clear rendering of the argument that pleasure and suffering come from habituation and are not ultimately real.

errors.english: If the Teacher, who knows all beings without exception, perceives emptiness,
errors.why: The phrase glosses 'empty of the Omniscient One': when people see the world empty of the all-knowing Teacher, some deluded ones cling to things as having essence; the Teacher does not perceive anything here.

fix.find: If the Teacher, who knows all beings without exception, perceives emptiness,
fix.replace: When they see [the world] empty of the Teacher, who knows all beings without exception,

errors.why: མེད་པའི completes བླ་ན་ from the previous side: 'by the Dharma and unsurpassed benefit', not 'selfless'.

note: The Vinaya glossary commentary (four truths, terms of debate) is mostly sound; one gloss reverses who sees the world as empty.
